next_steps: Redwood to send POC proposal + pricing for hosted and dedicated options (Maya) - by 2026-06-04
Customer to provide representative sample dataset and expected QPS numbers (Priya) - by 2026-06-04
SE to share benchmark harness and run plan; schedule load window with Horizon infra (Luis) - by 2026-06-05
Customer security to review SOC2 & KMS docs; Redwood to provide SOC2 report and controls contact (Aisha/Maya) - by 2026-06-06
action_items: Maya Chen: send pricing and dedicated capacity options by 2026-06-04
Luis Alvarez: prepare benchmark script and small load harness by 2026-06-05
Priya Singh: provide representative dataset, throughput targets, and success criteria by 2026-06-04

summary: POC scoping call focused on choosing between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment for Horizon Payments' payment-assist and fraud-detection ML features. Discussed success criteria (latency/throughput/accuracy), workload size, benchmark plan, timeline (2-week POC + decision), and security/compliance constraints (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: success criteria: p95 latency, throughput (QPS), accuracy/regression thresholds
workload sizing: convo length distribution, embedding volume, token counts
benchmarks: latency vs throughput tradeoffs, batching, KV cache reuse
timelines: 2-week POC plan and decision gating
security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency and retention
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this one. Luis from our SE team is here too. Uh quick roll call?
00:10 Speaker 2 (Priya): Priya Singh here, Head of ML at Horizon Payments.
00:14 Speaker 3 (Tom): Tom Baker, infra, I'll be helping with the benchmarks.
00:18 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Aisha Rahman, CISO.
00:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, thanks. Goal for today is to scope a POC to help you decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. We'll cover success criteria, workload size, benchmarks and timelines.
00:35 Speaker 2 (Priya): Sounds good. High level context: we run two LLM features. One is a payment-assist chat that surfaces payment options and helps customers with disputes; the other is a fraud scoring assistant that generates explanations for flagged transactions. Latency is pretty important for chat, p95 ideally under 200ms, but for fraud scoring batch jobs we're okay with higher latency. Throughput varies — chat is about 25-50 QPS peak, embeddings pipeline is about 200 calls per minute but asynchronous.
01:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): Helpful. Do you currently host anything on prem or mostly cloud?
01:08 Speaker 3 (Tom): We're cloud-first; infra in GCP with VPC controls. We may need data residency in EU for some flows. Also security will want KMS integration and audit logs.
01:18 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Yes, and we need to confirm key rotation policies, HSM where appropriate, SOC2 evidence, and SSO/SAML for RBAC.
01:26 Speaker 2 (Priya): From model perspective we plan to run a mix: a smaller chat model for interactive latency-sensitive paths and a larger reranker/embedding model for analytics. We may consider quantized variants (int8) to reduce cost.
01:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): OK, that's exactly the kind of tradeoff where Hosted can be fastest to get going, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost, and Private helps when the CISO needs everything in customer network or air-gapped. Luis, want to outline the benchmark plan?
01:52 Speaker 5 (Luis): Sure. Proposed POC: 2 weeks. Week 0 — prep and data handoff; Week 1 — baseline runs on Hosted using representative queries (mix of short chat prompts, mid-length 200-400 token prompts, and embedding calls), measure p95 latency, average latency, token throughput and cost per 1k tokens. We also measure model quality regression on a small eval set. Week 2 — spin up Dedicated pool configured to match expected concurrency and run same harness; if Private is required we'll plan for a parallel run but that's longer lead time. We'll collect trace-level logs and token-level cost breakdowns.
02:32 Speaker 2 (Priya): For success criteria: p95 chat latency <200ms for the 90% of requests, tail spikes acceptable within 300ms; cost target is within 30% of our current baseline (we're measuring now), and quality delta no more than 2% on our regression metric. Also we want clear audit logs and key management.
02:52 Speaker 3 (Tom): For infrastructure constraints: Our VPC requires static egress IP allow-listing; if you're hosted we need fixed ranges or the dedicated offering. Also we'll need RBAC integration to limit who can call which endpoints.
03:05 Speaker 5 (Luis): Notes — Redwood Dedicated supports fixed capacity pools and we can expose static egress IPs via NAT gateway in the dedicated config, and Redwood Private gives you customer-managed control plane inside your VPC. There may be an extra lead time for Private deployment and an enterprise agreement.
03:22 Speaker 4 (Aisha): How about encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS key separation per environment?
03:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): Encryption in transit by default, at rest encryption with KMS. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) and can integrate with GCP KMS/HSM. We'll share SOC2 report and our controls matrix after the call.
03:43 Speaker 2 (Priya): Benchmarks — how do you handle KV cache and batching? In chat we want prefix caching to reduce cost; for embeddings caching is less relevant.
03:53 Speaker 5 (Luis): Runtime supports KV cache reuse and smart batching. For the POC we'll measure with and without prefix caching enabled to show delta. Also we'll test quantized model variants for cost/perf tradeoffs. Note — some words in logs may show kv-cache spelled different, sorry if transcription later is odd.
04:12 Speaker 2 (Priya): Timeline — 2 weeks workable, but we need Redwood to provide the harness quickly. Tom and I can open a maintenance window for load runs.
04:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll get that out. For the POC decision criteria, would you accept Hosted if it meets latency and security reqs, or is Dedicated required?
04:29 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hosted is preferable for speed, but if we can't get the SLAs or static IPs we will need Dedicated. Private only if security team still has unresolved concerns.
04:38 Speaker 4 (Aisha): Private will be considered if we need total network control or specific data residency not achievable via hosted regions. Generally we'd prefer Dedicated over Private unless required.
04:48 Speaker 5 (Luis): Right, and Dedicated offers predictable unit economics with reserved pools; Hosted is usage-based and simpler. We'll make cost estimates for both.
04:57 Speaker 2 (Priya): On datasets — we'll provide 5000 sample chat prompts, 2000 embedding inputs and a small labeled eval set for reranker quality.
05:07 Speaker 3 (Tom): I'll coordinate the network allow-list and give you an ops contact.
05:11 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Any blockers?
05:14 Speaker 4 (Aisha): We just need SOC2 and the initial KMS integration docs. Also the compliance team will want to see data retention controls.
05:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll send SOC2 and our controls matrix. We'll also include a draft SLA and the dedicated capacity pricing sheet.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Priya): Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
05:32 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap: Redwood to send POC plan and pricing by Thursday, SE to send benchmark harness and propose load windows, Horizon to share datasets and QPS targets, security to review SOC2 artifacts. Decision after a 2-week POC.
05:47 Speaker 2 (Priya): Thanks, appreciate it.
05:49 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and set the schedule.
05:53 Speaker 3 (Tom): bye
05:54 Speaker 4 (Aisha): bye
05:55 Speaker 5 (Luis): bye
